Inaugurated 3 July 2026 by the President (TechAfrica gives 4 July); the Presidency calls it certified to Tier III standards without naming the certifying body. Floor space is the site ('more than 3,000 m2'); phase 1 has a 65 m2 colocation room. 1 MW is installed electrical capacity, not an IT-only figure, with phased increases planned; about 22% of energy from on-site solar. ITWeb says it connects to the ACE and SAT-3 cables and to national operators by peering; a room is set aside for AI uses. APDPVP authorised the site under Gabon's data-protection law after an impact study (September 2026) and says a mirror site is planned in Haut-Ogooue. The minister called it a private data centre (31 July 2026); ITWeb says the partnership structure with the state was not disclosed. ST Digital's own press page (4 July 2026) names the operating company ST Digital Data Center Services, a subsidiary of the ST Digital group, and gives 160 racks on a 4,000 m2 site against Seneweb's 92 racks. ST Digital's Gabon page lists ISO 27001, TIA-942 and HDS for its Douala, Grand-Bassam and Nkok sites; ISO 27001 is held at group level (March 2026). A private room can host AI infrastructure; no GPU hardware is named.

name: Geek Zone Data Center PLC (Holeta)
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

name: Dalkom Somalia Mogadishu Data Center
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Dalkom House, AMISOM Compound, Airport Road, Mogadishu. Status rests on its website (retrieved September 2026) and that entry.

name: South Sudan National Data Centre (MICT&PS)
operator: Ministry of Information, Communication Technology and Postal Services
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: The ministry announced in October 2024 that it would build the country's first resilient data centre, with World Bank resources, to host public- and private-sector data. name: Vodacom Mozambique Maputo Rooftop Data Centre
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Flexenclosure eCentre of three 42 sqm prefabricated modules on the helipad of a six-storey building in central Maputo, finished in May 2013 in eight days as Vodacom Mozambique's disaster recovery centre for mission-critical data and telecom equipment (IT News Africa, May 2013; STULZ project page, 174 kW cooling). Floor space is the modules' total. Distinct from the 500 sqm eCentre switching centre in Matola (MOZ-004). No source after 2014 says whether it is still in use. DCD (September 2013) places the modules on the helipad of Vodacom's regional office in central Maputo; no source after 2014 was found on whether it still runs.

name: NetOne NDC1
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: NetOne markets NDC1 as a purpose-built data centre with 'fault-tolerant Tier III certification', presence of major telcos, per-rack 3 kVA online UPS and generator backup; no Uptime Institute record was checked. PeeringDB lists the facility as NetOne Data Lusaka with networks present (read 21 September 2026) and describes it as multi-tenant and carrier-neutral. No Uptime Institute award for NetOne was found.

name: MTN Business Zambia Lusaka Data Centre
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Listed by OCOLO as an MTN Business colocation site on Danny Pule Road, Lusaka, with no specifications. MTN Zambia is an MTN Group subsidiary; its shareholding is not sourced here.

name: TelOne Mazowe Data Centre (Mazowe Earth Station)
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: At the Mazowe Earth Station north of Harare. Opened with TelOne's Harare data centre in March 2017 under the National Broadband project, funded by a $98M China Exim Bank loan and built with Huawei (DCD, 2017). A US$1M extension commissioned in March 2022 added a fourth Performance Optimised Data Centre module, taking it from 14 to 34 racks and 300 kW of IT load (263Chat; TechnoMag); investment_usd is that extension only. TelOne names banks, telcos and government departments among its customers (TechnoMag, March 2022). At the Mazowe expansion launch TelOne's chairman said the new module lets customers including government departments take disaster recovery hosting there (TechnoMag, March 2022).

name: TelOne Bulawayo Data Centre
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Commissioned 28 April 2022 in Bulawayo CBD with a customer experience centre at Hillside; 120 racks and 400 kVA, Tier III by design (not certified), the first data centre in Matabeleland (Techzim; Ecofin; TechnoMag). DCmag says it is mainly equipped by Huawei; 400 kVA is the power rating reported, not IT load. DCD and DCmag give the power as 400 kW, Techzim and Ecofin as 400 kVA; none says it is IT load.

name: Airtel Malawi Blantyre Data Centre
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Opened in Blantyre in December 2013 with over US$1M invested, doubling Airtel Malawi's capacity to host its own ICT systems, with cloud services promised (DCD, 3 December 2013). investment_usd is 'over $1m' as reported. No later source on the site was found. Commissioned at Airtel's head offices in Limbe, Blantyre (Nyasa Times, November 2013). The 2025 presentation names Blantyre as the primary data centre and Lilongwe as disaster recovery; it does not say whether this is the 2013 build.

name: Paratus Swakopmund Cable Landing Station (Equiano)
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Built by Paratus as landing party, with Telecom Namibia as infrastructure partner, under a February 2021 agreement with Google; the building was finished in June-September 2021, fit-out (power, cabinets, cages, security) in January 2022, and the cable landed on 1 July 2022 (ITWeb; Submarine Networks). The station is also a meeting point where operators collect and distribute capacity. DCD (2023) says Armada (NAM-001) acts as the landing station; ITWeb and Paratus place it in Swakopmund, and Armada is the Windhoek data centre it backhauls to. Paratus Namibia Holdings' 2025 integrated report puts the station on Erf 3560, Swakopmund, a 1,000 m2 plot, and gives the building's cost as N$29,691,662 excluding the internal fit-out; investment_usd converts that at about N$14.79 to the dollar, the 2021 average, when the building was put up.

name: BDIH Data Centre (Botswana Digital & Innovation Hub)
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: In the Hub's building at Plot 69184, Block 8, Science and Technology Park, Gaborone: 80 racks, Tier III compliant by the Hub's own description (not certified), two power circuits, UPS and two generators, a meet-me room with BoFiNet, VBN and BTC connected; tenants bring their own servers and internet. Uptime Institute lists a 'Government Integrated Data Centre 1 (GIDC 1), Phase 1' for the Hub as client, which may be this facility. Separate from BoFiNet's Digital Delta Data Centre (BWA-002) on its own plot in the same park. No source found ties Uptime's GIDC 1 award, whose client is the Hub and whose award type is not shown, to this data centre, or gives its opening year.

name: Government of Lesotho Primary Data Centre (Ministry of Finance, Maseru)
operator: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: The government's primary data centre at the Ministry of Finance in Maseru, which the Mohale's Hoek site (LSO-003) backs up (Government of Lesotho, May 2018). In 2025 the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning awarded Mapota Technologies a three-year LSL 35.6M contract to replace end-of-life government data hosting equipment and build a public-sector business continuity framework under the World Bank's Public Sector Foundations project (P174171), which is the status source. MoFDP's terms of reference for the IFMIS upgrade (c. 2025) say the IFMIS servers bought in 2018 are still in operation, serving all ministries; it does not name the building, and no opening year was found.

name: Sonangol Corporate Data Centre (Luanda)
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Inaugurated 25 February 2026 for Sonangol's 50th anniversary; consolidates data centres previously spread across its subsidiaries. 920 m2 is the building (administration, SOC, NOC, UPS and communications rooms); the data hall is 400 m2, 182 m2 in use (Angop, PTI). Site within Luanda not stated. Separate from MSTelcom's data centres (AGO-005 to AGO-007), a Sonangol subsidiary.

name: Ministry of Finance Data Centre (Ngaliema, Kinshasa)
operator: Ministry of Finance of the DRC
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

Built by Huawei under a December 2017 contract amended in 2020, with financing through cooperation with China. 54 servers, 1,278 TB of storage, two 480 kVA generators (Primature). Distinct from the government data centre in the Immeuble du Gouvernement, Gombe (COD-005). Financed by a USD 150 million China EXIM loan for the finance ministry's modernisation project, approved by Ordinance 20/130 of 31 July 2020 (AfricaNews RDC; Xinhua).

name: Lofoy HPC Data Centre (Université Nouveaux Horizons)
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Inaugurated 27 June 2026 on the Université Nouveaux Horizons campus: two rooms, one holding 4 racks (30 servers) plus storage servers, with a control room (La Guardia, DecryptEco, RFI via Africain Times). Aimed at research and AI; the university plans to rent storage to banks, miners and public bodies.

source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
note: Directory listings (Inflect, DataCenterJournal) place Airtel's Libreville data centre at Rue Pecqueur, Libreville Business Square, offering cabinets, cages and connectivity; DCD (2025) lists Airtel Gabon among Libreville's existing data centres. Listings are undated.

name: Zanzibar National Data Centre (ZICTIA)
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

Correction: ZIBI lists the US$75m, 200-rack, 2 MW Tier III centre among ZICTIA's upcoming projects, so it is a planned facility, not this site. UN DESA (January 2013) reports President Shein launching an e-government centre at Mazizini built with China's ZTE among suppliers; The Citizen (August 2018) says a data centre for Zanzibar's hospitals had been completed at Mazizini. Neither says which date is this data centre's opening. Zanzibar's communications minister said on 2 October 2026 that more than TZS 53 billion is set aside for three ICT infrastructure projects, chiefly a data centre and public internet; he named no site, capacity or completion date.

name: Lumitel Bujumbura
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

No site, capacity, services or opening year published. Lumitel's Stevie Awards entry (January 2025) lists a ServerCloud server-rental service among its ICT products; whether the data centres also sell colocation is not stated.

name: Guinea-Bissau National Data Centre (Alto Bandim)
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

Completion not reported by September 2026. Mais Afrika (29 March 2024) gives EUR 1.93M from Japan for the ITMA headquarters building that will house the data centre; neither figure is for the data centre alone. Completion by the July 2026 target is not reported.

name: Orange Liberia Buchanan Tier III+ Data Centre
source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
